title: Verbatim legal quotation check, second blind set (40 quotations from 1973 opinions)

not_shipped.reason: the script that built the set from the public texts. It names the authors' internal folders and a private user-agent string, so the export that assembles this public tree refuses it, and it is withheld. What it produced ships: the 39 opinion texts in sources/opinions/ (and the same texts without their header line in sources/opinions-unheaded/), each pinned by sha256 in items/MANIFEST.json, and the items themselves. The raw Caselaw Access Project files it read (about 48 MB of JSON) are not shipped; each is pinned by URL, fetch time and sha256 in sources/fetch-log.jsonl. rerun.mjs reruns every step of the run from the shipped texts with the package's engine and compares the outcomes with results/.

rerun.detail: The 39 opinion texts ship in sources/ (headed and unheaded), pinned by sha256 in items/MANIFEST.json. From the repository root, after npm install && npm run build, node packages/verify/docs/bench/legal-blind-2/rerun.mjs reruns half A, the tuning search, half B and the unheaded step with the package's engine and compares every case with results/; on 2026-10-06 every outcome the table counts was identical (160 of 160, and the tuning search's values and chosen limits). Two things differ and the script says so: the verdict ids and some explanation wording, because today's engine is not the build the run used (its sources are hashed below), and rerun.mjs was written after the run in place of harness/run.ts, which imports the authors' working tree. The script that built the texts from the raw Caselaw Access Project files does not ship (it names the authors' folders); the raw files are pinned by URL, time and sha256 in sources/fetch-log.jsonl.

run.blind_basis: PREREG.sha256 records the prereg's sha256 at 2026-10-05T14:00:36Z, and sources/fetch-log.jsonl records all 110 fetches of the opinion texts between 14:03:28Z and 14:06:31Z, after it; the built set and the harness were hashed at 14:26:01Z, nine seconds before the run. Both files were written by the authors, and the AI agent that wrote the prereg also built the set and audited it

misses.description: L2-03: a genuine-quotation item whose label is wrong: the quotation is from a federal appeals opinion in 454 F. 2d (a short form "454 F. 2d, at 584" the citation filter missed), and the next U.S. cite was the quoting case's own certiorari grant, so the source is the wrong opinion. Every rule abstained, which is the right answer, but it counts against the genuine rate

L2-05: a genuine-quotation item whose label is wrong: the cite taken is the quoting case's own certiorari grant (405 U.S. 974): the source is an order, not the quoted opinion. Every rule abstained, which is the right answer, but it counts against the genuine rate

L2-07: a genuine-quotation item whose label is wrong: the cite taken names the case the quotation is about ("upheld in Vuitch", 402 U.S. 62), not the quotation's source. Every rule abstained, which is the right answer, but it counts against the genuine rate

L2-21: a genuine-quotation item whose label is wrong: the quotation is a statute (28 U.S.C. § 2241(a)); the statute citation was not filtered, so the source is the wrong text. Every rule abstained, which is the right answer, but it counts against the genuine rate

L2-27: a genuine-quotation item whose label is wrong: the cite taken is an order setting argument (409 U.S. 974), not the quoted opinion. Every rule abstained, which is the right answer, but it counts against the genuine rate

the build harness's "next citation" filter let order cites, a statute and a cite inside the quoted subject through; it caused all five label errors. A next set should take only a citation that directly follows the closing mark and exclude orders and memorandum decisions

the known-bad operators (altered, elided, fabricated, bracket-changed) produce neither a later opinion's text that cites the case nor a condition cut off at the start or end of a quotation; an outside reviewer's 26-citation brief found eight such quotations legal@0.2.0 passed (three wrong-opinion, five edge or untriggered conditions), so this set's 0 of 20 known-bad passes measures its generator, not those kinds
